title: Hierarchical time-bucketed fragmentation scheduler and KV steering for continuous-batching
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem statement: GPU-resident KV caches are suffering from progressive fragmentation under mixed workloads (short chat sessions + long generation tails). Fragmentation increases memory pressure, leads to frequent compaction, and causes latency P99 spikes when compaction collides with hot request paths.

Goal: Implement a hierarchical time-bucketed fragmentation scheduler paired with an allocation steering layer that biases new allocations to 'write lanes' per GPU region. The scheduler batches compaction/eviction work into bounded windows (time buckets) with hysteresis and rate-limits to avoid interfering with low-latency continuous-batching. Expected outcome: reduce background compaction tail events, improve median and P99 latency stability, and lower token-cost per GPU by improving cache hit locality.

Scope in this ticket: design and prototype the scheduler and steering logic, integrate with the runtime's allocation hooks, add telemetry and safety toggles, and ship a runtime feature flag for canary testing on Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads (link in 'links')
Prototype implemented and runs in perf lab with synthetic mixed workload harness
Measured improvements: >25% reduction in compaction-triggered latency spikes (P99) under mixed workload profile compared to baseline
Feature flag with rollout controls (per-cluster) and two safety toggles: max_compaction_bandwidth and compaction_cooldown_ms
Telemetry: per-GPU time-bucket compaction counts, allocation lane occupancy, KV fragmentation heatmap, and end-to-end latency correlation dashboard
implementation_notes: Design: maintain 3 hierarchical tiers: hot, warm, cold. Each tier maintains independent time buckets (e.g., 500ms windows) to schedule background consolidation work.
Allocation steering: new KV slabs preferentially allocated into active lanes within a tier. Lanes are coarse-grained (e.g., 4 lanes per GPU) to reduce allocator metadata and enable fast bulk moves.
Hysteresis & cooldown: once a lane is chosen for consolidation, apply a cooldown to avoid repeated compactions (tunable hysteresis).

Continuous-batching integration: scheduler consults current batching pressure: if in high-throughput low-latency mode, shift compaction to lower-priority buckets and reduce concurrency to maintain latency SLOs.
Eviction windows: instead of immediate per-request eviction, mark candidates and coalesce removals into the next bucket; this improves locality by freeing contiguous ranges.
Fallback behavior: if fragmentation crosses emergency threshold, fall back to conservative full-slab compaction with rate-limit and alerting.
Resource controls: compaction tasks are cgrouped and limited to configured GPU memory copy bandwidth and CPU concurrency to avoid starving inference threads.
